_comment: Copy this file to sqreader.config.json (gitignored) and edit as needed.
Every value here is a DEFAULT; a matching CLI flag always wins over it.
On a standard single-instance box you usually need NO config at all: the
Squad server is found by its process name and output dirs default next to
the repo. Only non-standard setups need to change anything below.
The file is loaded from $SQREADER_CONFIG, else ./sqreader.config.json.
_discovery_comment: Which game server does THIS reader read? One reader = one game server =
one data directory. Two servers on one host need two configs, two
server_id values and two data directories; the reader refuses to start on
a data directory whose stats DB already holds another server_id.
NEVER pin a PID (no --pid $(pidof ...), no PID in a unit or config): PIDs
are transient. The reader finds the game by criteria and re-discovers it
after every restart. `--pid` still works but is verified (game binary +
these criteria) and refused otherwise.
squad_port / squad_query_port: the game's -Port= / -QueryPort= (also found
inside UE '?Port=' URL arguments; whole-number match). Use whichever you
know; the reader reports which key matched. With neither, more than one
game process on the host is an ERROR (nothing is chosen for you).
expected_container_id: 64-hex Docker container id or a prefix of at least
12 characters. Optional extra check. Re-creating the container changes the
id: update this value then, or the reader refuses the new process (and says
so in its log and /health/deep).
log_path_in_container: where the game writes its log INSIDE the container;
read through /proc/<pid>/root (needs root or equivalent). Default:
/home/container/SquadGame/Saved/Logs/SquadGame.log. log_path is an explicit
path on the reader's own filesystem and wins over everything.
_plugins_comment: Plugins are off unless a config path is given. --plugins-config wins;
this key is the fallback for deployments whose start command is not
yours to edit. The file it points at is {plugin_id: {enabled, config}}.
_alerts_comment: Plugin alerts (see --plugins-config) always land in the stats database.
Set alert_webhook to a Discord webhook URL to have them announced there
as well. That URL is a CREDENTIAL - anyone holding it can post in the
channel - which is why it lives here and not on a command line other
users on the box can read out of `ps`.
alert_replay_base builds a 'watch the replay' link on each alert; without
it the alert still arrives, just with no way to go and look. null (the
default) = no link: this fork points at no external site.
alert_min_confidence keeps the noisy end of a detector in the database
without putting it in a channel humans are expected to read.
_multi_instance_comment: Running SEVERAL Squad servers on one box? Set squad_port (or
squad_query_port) to the one THIS agent reads and give each agent its own
server_id and data directory. Without a port criterion the reader refuses
to start while more than one game process exists. Each instance also needs
its own install dir, HTTP port and systemd unit: see the installer's
_net_comment: LOCAL MODE (default): net_policy=local-only. This reader opens NO outbound
connection to any external service: no central platform, no update or
offset-pack server, no chat webhook on the internet. Only loopback, private
(RFC1918 / CGNAT / unique-local) addresses and hosts listed VERBATIM in
net_allow_hosts are reachable (no wildcards, no implied subdomains).
Under local-only `sqreader enroll` refuses (exit code 2) without touching
the network and the push below is inert.
net_policy=allow-central restores the upstream behaviour (enroll, push,
check-in, offset packs, self-update) and must be chosen explicitly.
win over these keys. `sqreader doctor` and /health/deep show the policy.
_push_comment: Optional central push. INERT in local mode (net_policy=local-only above):
nothing is sent and the reader says 'merkezi gönderim kapalı (yerel mod)'.
It only does anything under net_policy=allow-central (or with the central
host listed in net_allow_hosts). Then it reports FINISHED matches (stats +
.sqrx replays; never the live map) to a central platform. Enroll first:
is stored in a 0600 .env.agent, NOT here. See PRIVACY.md.
push_replay: also upload the match replay (set false for stats-only).
push_backlog_dir: pending-push queue (default: next to the stats DB).
update_enabled / offset_autoheal (both false by default here) fetch signed
releases / offset packs from that central: leave them false in local mode.
_export_comment: Optional Export API v1 (OFF by default): a read-only, token-protected pull
interface (GET /export/v1/*) that hands FINISHED matches and their replays
to a consumer such as Zero Zone. export_token_file is the PATH of a file
holding the bearer token (at least 32 characters, chmod 600) - the token
itself never goes in this config. Unset, missing, empty or short = the
API is off and every /export/v1/* path answers 404.
Two POST endpoints (same token, Content-Type: application/json, body <= 4 KB)
are the only writes: /export/v1/control/recording switches NEW recordings
on/off (an open recording is never cut; stats keep flowing) and
/export/v1/ack tells the reader which recordings the consumer has mirrored.
Both are audited in export_audit.log. export_state_dir = where
_retention_comment: run by the daily timer) and the recorder's low-disk guard. 0 = limit off.
Only FINALIZED recordings are ever removed. With the Export API on
(retention_require_ack null = auto), age / size rules remove only recordings
the consumer ACKED. An un-acked recording goes only in a disk EMERGENCY
(free space below retention_min_free_gb), oldest first, with a WARNING and an
audit-log line. The active recording, unverified / legacy ones (unless
retention_include_unverified and their own longer age limit) and anything
modified in the last retention_in_progress_min minutes are never touched.
When free space is below retention_min_free_gb and nothing can be freed, NO
new recording is opened (health: recordingEnabledReason=disk_low); stats
collection and the game server are unaffected. `retention --dry-run` lists
what would go and why. Placeholders below: tune to your disk.
